_about: Major discoveries and inventions with the place where they were made, written for GeoHistory from general knowledge (AI-written text, shown with that label). Each entry names its English Wikipedia article. 'place' is the town where the work was done or first shown; the state is never written here: tools/context/build_discoveries.py looks the place up on the map of that year, so Gutenberg's Mainz press of 1450 belongs to whatever the map shows at Mainz in 1450, not to today's Germany. 'state' is given only for voyages and works without one place (the sponsoring state). The year is checked against the article's Wikidata item (time of discovery or invention P575, inception P571, publication date P577, point in time P585 or start time P580; 1 year of slack, 25 for 'approx') and the result written to 'verified'.

discoveries.name: Telephone
discoveries.text: Bell was granted US patent 174,465 on 7 March 1876 and made the first call to his assistant Thomas Watson in Boston three days later.
discoveries.note: Elisha Gray filed a caveat for a similar telephone at the patent office on the same day as Bell's application (14 February 1876); Antonio Meucci had demonstrated a 'telettrofono' and filed a caveat in 1871 but could not renew it.

discoveries.name: Movable-type printing press
discoveries.text: Gutenberg combined metal movable type, oil-based ink and a screw press in Mainz around 1450; his Bible was finished by about 1455.
discoveries.note: Movable type itself was older: Bi Sheng's ceramic type in Song China (about 1040) and metal type in Goryeo Korea (Jikji, 1377).

discoveries.name: Penicillin
discoveries.text: Fleming noticed in September 1928 that a Penicillium mould killed the bacteria around it; Florey and Chain's team in Oxford made it a usable drug from 1940.

discoveries.name: Newcomen atmospheric engine
discoveries.text: The first known working steam engine pumped water from a coal mine near Dudley Castle in 1712.

discoveries.name: Watt steam engine
discoveries.text: Watt's separate condenser (patented 1769) cut the fuel a steam engine needed; the first Boulton and Watt engines went to work in 1776.

discoveries.name: Incandescent light bulb (Edison)
discoveries.text: Edison's team made a carbon-filament lamp that burned for hours in October 1879 and showed it publicly at Menlo Park that December.
discoveries.note: Joseph Swan made working carbon lamps in Newcastle at the same time; the two later merged their British companies as Ediswan.

discoveries.name: X-rays
discoveries.text: Röntgen found the new rays on 8 November 1895 and published in December, with an X-ray of his wife's hand.

discoveries.name: First powered aeroplane flight (Wright Flyer)
discoveries.text: On 17 December 1903 the Wright Flyer made four controlled, powered flights, the longest 260 m in 59 seconds.

discoveries.name: Papermaking (Cai Lun)
discoveries.text: The court official Cai Lun presented a paper made of bark, hemp and rags to the Han emperor in 105.
discoveries.note: Archaeology has found older paper in China (2nd century BC); Cai Lun improved and standardised the process.

discoveries.name: Telescope
discoveries.text: The spectacle-maker Lipperhey applied for a patent on a telescope in The Hague in October 1608; it was refused because others made them too.

discoveries.name: Smallpox vaccine
discoveries.text: Jenner inoculated James Phipps with cowpox in May 1796 and showed that it protected him from smallpox.

discoveries.name: Dynamite
discoveries.text: Nobel stabilised nitroglycerine in kieselguhr at his factory in Krümmel near Hamburg and patented the result as dynamite in 1867.

discoveries.name: Special relativity
discoveries.text: Einstein, then a patent clerk in Bern, published 'On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies' in 1905, his 'miracle year'.

discoveries.name: General relativity
discoveries.text: Einstein presented the field equations of general relativity to the Prussian Academy in Berlin in November 1915.

discoveries.name: Double-helix structure of DNA
discoveries.wiki: Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid
discoveries.text: Watson and Crick published the double helix in Nature in April 1953.
discoveries.note: Their model rested on X-ray data from Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins at King's College London, published in the same issue.

discoveries.name: Sputnik 1
discoveries.text: The first artificial satellite was launched on 4 October 1957 and orbited for three weeks of radio signals.

discoveries.name: Nuclear fission
discoveries.text: Hahn and Strassmann found barium among the products of uranium bombarded with neutrons in December 1938.
discoveries.note: Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch, in exile, explained it as the splitting of the nucleus in early 1939.

discoveries.name: Transistor
discoveries.who: John Bardeen, Walter Brattain and William Shockley
discoveries.text: The point-contact transistor was first shown working at Bell Labs on 16 December 1947.

discoveries.name: Insulin as a treatment
discoveries.text: Banting and Best isolated insulin at the University of Toronto in 1921; the first patient was treated in January 1922.

discoveries.name: Phonograph
discoveries.text: Edison's tinfoil phonograph, the first machine to record and play back sound, was built in late 1877.

discoveries.name: Benz Patent-Motorwagen (first automobile)
discoveries.text: Benz built his three-wheeled petrol car in 1885 and patented it in January 1886; Bertha Benz drove it to Pforzheim in 1888.

discoveries.name: World Wide Web
discoveries.text: Berners-Lee proposed a hypertext information system at CERN in March 1989; the first web server ran there in 1990.

discoveries.name: First written gunpowder formula
discoveries.text: The military manual Wujing Zongyao, compiled for the Song court, gives the earliest known formulas for gunpowder.
discoveries.note: Gunpowder itself was found by Chinese alchemists earlier, probably in the 9th century.

discoveries.name: First steam railway locomotive journey
discoveries.text: Trevithick's locomotive hauled 10 tons of iron and 70 men along the Penydarren tramway on 21 February 1804.

discoveries.name: Stephenson's Rocket
discoveries.text: Rocket won the Rainhill Trials of October 1829 and set the pattern of later steam locomotives.

discoveries.name: Morse telegraph line
discoveries.text: Morse sent 'What hath God wrought' from the Capitol in Washington to Baltimore on 24 May 1844.
discoveries.note: Cooke and Wheatstone had patented a working electrical telegraph in Britain in 1837.

discoveries.name: First photograph
discoveries.wiki: View from the Window at Le Gras
discoveries.text: Niépce's 'View from the Window at Le Gras' (1826 or 1827) is the oldest surviving camera photograph.

discoveries.name: Daguerreotype
discoveries.text: The French Academy of Sciences announced Daguerre's process in January 1839; it was the first practical photography.

discoveries.name: Radio (wireless telegraphy)
discoveries.text: Marconi sent wireless signals over more than a kilometre at his family's estate in 1895, then patented his system in Britain in 1896.
discoveries.note: Many contributed: Hertz (radio waves, 1886-1888), Lodge, Popov, Bose and Tesla.

discoveries.name: Moons of Jupiter (Galileo)
discoveries.text: With his own telescope Galileo saw four moons circling Jupiter in January 1610 and published them in Sidereus Nuncius that March.

discoveries.name: Copernican heliocentrism
discoveries.text: Copernicus, a canon of Frombork, put the Sun at the centre of the planets' orbits in De revolutionibus, printed in Nuremberg in 1543.

discoveries.name: Newton's laws of motion and gravitation
discoveries.text: Newton's Principia (1687) set out the laws of motion and universal gravitation.

discoveries.name: Evolution by natural selection
discoveries.text: Darwin published On the Origin of Species in November 1859, a year after he and Alfred Russel Wallace presented the theory jointly.

discoveries.name: Periodic table
discoveries.text: Mendeleev arranged the elements by atomic weight in 1869 and left gaps for elements not yet found.

discoveries.name: Rabies vaccine
discoveries.text: Pasteur's team gave the vaccine to nine-year-old Joseph Meister, bitten by a rabid dog, in July 1885; he survived.

discoveries.name: Radioactivity
discoveries.text: Becquerel found in 1896 that uranium salts fogged photographic plates without light.

discoveries.name: Polonium and radium
discoveries.text: The Curies announced polonium in July and radium in December 1898, found in pitchblende.

discoveries.name: Electron
discoveries.text: Thomson showed in 1897 that cathode rays are made of particles far lighter than atoms.

discoveries.name: Electromagnetic induction
discoveries.text: Faraday showed in August 1831 that a changing magnetic field makes an electric current, the principle of the dynamo.
discoveries.note: Joseph Henry found the same effect independently in the United States.

discoveries.name: Voltaic pile (electric battery)
discoveries.text: Volta described the first electric battery, a stack of zinc and copper discs, in a letter to the Royal Society in 1800.

discoveries.name: Lightning rod and the kite experiment
discoveries.text: Franklin's kite experiment of 1752 supported his claim that lightning is electricity, and he promoted lightning rods.

discoveries.name: Cotton gin
discoveries.text: Whitney's gin (1793, patented 1794) separated cotton fibre from seed quickly, making short-staple cotton profitable and spreading slavery in the American South.

discoveries.name: Spinning jenny
discoveries.text: Hargreaves' multi-spindle spinning frame (about 1764) let one worker spin eight or more threads at once.

discoveries.name: Flying shuttle
discoveries.text: Kay's flying shuttle (1733) doubled a weaver's output.

discoveries.name: First crewed balloon flight
discoveries.who: Montgolfier brothers; Pilâtre de Rozier and the Marquis d'Arlandes
discoveries.text: On 21 November 1783 a Montgolfier hot-air balloon carried two men over Paris for about 25 minutes.

discoveries.name: Commercial steamboat (Clermont)
discoveries.text: Fulton's steamboat ran from New York to Albany up the Hudson in August 1807, starting the first commercial steamboat service.

discoveries.name: Surgical anaesthesia with ether
discoveries.text: Morton anaesthetised a patient with ether for an operation in public on 16 October 1846.

discoveries.name: Four-stroke engine (Otto)
discoveries.text: Otto built the first practical four-stroke internal combustion engine in 1876.

discoveries.name: Public film screening (Lumière Cinématographe)
discoveries.text: The Lumières showed ten short films to a paying audience in Paris on 28 December 1895.

discoveries.name: Television (Baird demonstration)
discoveries.text: Baird gave the first public demonstration of moving television images in his Soho laboratory on 26 January 1926.

discoveries.name: First jet aircraft flight (Heinkel He 178)
discoveries.who: Hans von Ohain and Erich Warsitz
discoveries.text: The He 178 made the first flight of a turbojet aircraft on 27 August 1939.
discoveries.note: Frank Whittle in Britain had run a jet engine on a test bench in 1937.

discoveries.name: ENIAC (electronic computer)
discoveries.who: John Mauchly and J. Presper Eckert
discoveries.text: ENIAC, the first programmable general-purpose electronic computer, was completed in late 1945 and unveiled in February 1946.

discoveries.name: First nuclear weapon test (Trinity)
discoveries.text: The Manhattan Project exploded the first atomic bomb on 16 July 1945.

discoveries.name: Polio vaccine (Salk)
discoveries.text: Salk's inactivated vaccine, developed at the University of Pittsburgh, was declared safe and effective on 12 April 1955 after a field trial of 1.8 million children.

discoveries.name: First human spaceflight (Vostok 1)
discoveries.text: Gagarin orbited the Earth once on 12 April 1961.

discoveries.name: First crewed Moon landing (Apollo 11)
discoveries.who: Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, Michael Collins
discoveries.text: Armstrong and Aldrin landed on the Moon on 20 July 1969 and walked on it for about two and a half hours.

discoveries.name: Laser
discoveries.text: Maiman built the first working laser, a ruby laser, in May 1960.

discoveries.name: Integrated circuit
discoveries.text: Kilby showed the first working integrated circuit on 12 September 1958.
discoveries.note: Robert Noyce at Fairchild made the first practical silicon (planar) integrated circuit in 1959.

discoveries.name: Microprocessor (Intel 4004)
discoveries.who: Federico Faggin, Ted Hoff, Stanley Mazor, Masatoshi Shima
discoveries.text: The Intel 4004, the first commercial microprocessor, went on sale in November 1971.

discoveries.name: ARPANET, forerunner of the Internet
discoveries.text: The first message between two ARPANET computers went from UCLA to Stanford Research Institute on 29 October 1969.

discoveries.name: Aspirin
discoveries.text: Bayer chemists made pure acetylsalicylic acid in 1897 and sold it as Aspirin from 1899.

discoveries.name: Antiseptic surgery
discoveries.text: Lister published his results with carbolic acid in 1867, sharply cutting deaths after surgery.

discoveries.name: ABO blood groups
discoveries.text: Landsteiner described the blood groups in 1901, which made safe transfusion possible.

discoveries.name: Quantum hypothesis (Planck)
discoveries.text: Planck's law of black-body radiation (December 1900) assumed that energy comes in quanta, the start of quantum physics.

discoveries.name: Microorganisms (Leeuwenhoek)
discoveries.text: With his own microscopes Leeuwenhoek described bacteria and other 'animalcules' to the Royal Society in 1676.

discoveries.name: Circulation of the blood
discoveries.text: Harvey showed in De Motu Cordis (1628) that the heart pumps blood round the body in a circuit.

discoveries.name: Pendulum clock
discoveries.text: Huygens built the first pendulum clock in 1656, making clocks accurate to about a minute a day.

discoveries.name: Mercury barometer
discoveries.text: Torricelli's mercury tube of 1643 showed that air has weight and measured its pressure.

discoveries.name: Logarithms
discoveries.text: Napier published his tables of logarithms in 1614, which made long calculations in astronomy and navigation far quicker.

discoveries.name: Rules for zero and negative numbers (Brahmagupta)
discoveries.text: Brahmagupta's treatise of 628 gives the first written rules for calculating with zero and negative numbers.

discoveries.name: Paper money (jiaozi)
discoveries.text: The Song government took over the merchants' paper notes of Sichuan and issued the first government paper money in 1024.

discoveries.name: Algebra (al-Khwarizmi)
discoveries.wiki: The Compendious Book on Calculation by Completion and Balancing
discoveries.text: Al-Khwarizmi's book on 'completion and balancing' (al-jabr), written in Baghdad around 820, gave algebra its name.

discoveries.name: Book of Optics (Ibn al-Haytham)
discoveries.text: Ibn al-Haytham showed by experiment that we see by light entering the eye; written in Cairo between 1011 and 1021.

discoveries.name: Measurement of the Earth (Eratosthenes)
discoveries.text: The librarian of Alexandria measured the Earth's circumference from the Sun's angle at Syene and Alexandria, around 240 BC.

discoveries.name: Seismoscope (Zhang Heng)
discoveries.text: Zhang Heng presented a seismoscope to the Han court in 132 that showed the direction of a distant earthquake.

discoveries.name: Columbus reaches the Americas
discoveries.text: Sailing for Castile, Columbus landed in the Bahamas on 12 October 1492, beginning lasting European contact with the Americas.
discoveries.note: Norse Greenlanders had reached Newfoundland about 1000 (L'Anse aux Meadows).

discoveries.name: Sea route to India (Vasco da Gama)
discoveries.text: Da Gama sailed round Africa and reached Calicut in May 1498, opening the sea route from Europe to India.

discoveries.name: First circumnavigation (Magellan-Elcano)
discoveries.who: Ferdinand Magellan and Juan Sebastián Elcano
discoveries.text: Of five ships that left Spain in 1519, one returned in September 1522 under Elcano, having sailed round the world; Magellan was killed in the Philippines.

discoveries.name: Cook charts eastern Australia
discoveries.text: Cook charted the east coast of Australia in 1770 and claimed it for Britain.

discoveries.name: Oxygen
discoveries.text: Priestley made oxygen by heating mercuric oxide on 1 August 1774.
discoveries.note: Carl Wilhelm Scheele had made it earlier (1771-1772) but published later; Lavoisier named it and explained its role in burning.

discoveries.name: Uranus
discoveries.text: Herschel saw Uranus from his garden in Bath on 13 March 1781, the first planet found with a telescope.

discoveries.name: Neptune
discoveries.who: Johann Galle, from Urbain Le Verrier's prediction
discoveries.text: Galle found Neptune at the Berlin Observatory on 23 September 1846, within a degree of where Le Verrier had calculated it.
discoveries.note: John Couch Adams in Cambridge had made a similar prediction.

discoveries.name: Laws of inheritance (Mendel)
discoveries.text: The friar Mendel presented his pea-plant experiments in Brno in 1865; they were ignored until 1900.

discoveries.name: Tuberculosis bacterium
discoveries.text: Koch announced on 24 March 1882 that a bacterium causes tuberculosis.

discoveries.name: Rosetta Stone
discoveries.text: French soldiers found the stone in July 1799; its Greek text was the key Champollion used to read hieroglyphs in 1822.

discoveries.name: Tomb of Tutankhamun
discoveries.text: Carter found the nearly intact tomb in November 1922.

discoveries.name: Liquid-fuelled rocket
discoveries.text: Goddard launched the first liquid-fuelled rocket on 16 March 1926; it flew 12 m high.

discoveries.name: Bakelite (first synthetic plastic)
discoveries.text: Baekeland made the first fully synthetic plastic in 1907.

discoveries.name: Ammonia synthesis (Haber process)
discoveries.text: Haber made ammonia from the nitrogen of the air in 1909; Carl Bosch scaled it up for fertiliser and explosives.

discoveries.name: Expanding universe (Hubble's law)
discoveries.text: Hubble showed in 1929 that the farther a galaxy is, the faster it moves away.
discoveries.note: Georges Lemaître had published the relation in 1927.

discoveries.name: Cosmic microwave background
discoveries.wiki: Discovery of cosmic microwave background radiation
discoveries.text: Penzias and Wilson found an unexplained microwave hiss from every direction in 1964, the afterglow of the Big Bang.

discoveries.name: First human heart transplant
discoveries.text: Barnard transplanted a heart into Louis Washkansky on 3 December 1967; he lived 18 days.

discoveries.name: First IVF birth
discoveries.text: Louise Brown, the first baby conceived by in vitro fertilisation, was born on 25 July 1978.

discoveries.name: Dolly the sheep (cloned mammal)
discoveries.text: Dolly, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, was born on 5 July 1996.

discoveries.name: Higgs boson
discoveries.text: CERN announced on 4 July 2012 that the Large Hadron Collider had found the particle predicted by Higgs and others in 1964.

discoveries.name: Gravitational waves detected
discoveries.text: LIGO detected waves from two merging black holes on 14 September 2015, as Einstein's theory predicted.

discoveries.name: Pulsars
discoveries.who: Jocelyn Bell Burnell and Antony Hewish
discoveries.text: Bell Burnell noticed the regular radio pulses of the first pulsar in November 1967.

discoveries.name: Diesel engine
discoveries.text: Diesel's compression-ignition engine (patented 1893) first ran efficiently at the Augsburg machine works in 1897.

discoveries.name: Pasteurisation
discoveries.text: Pasteur showed in 1864 that gentle heating kept wine from spoiling by killing microbes.
